questions.question_text: In how many ways can $7$ people be seated around a circular table, assuming rotations are equivalent?

options.why: Calculated 7!, assuming a linear arrangement instead of a circular arrangement.
Calculated (7 - 2)! = 5! instead of (7 - 1)! = 6!.
Divided by 2, incorrectly assuming reflections are equivalent for people at a table.

questions.question_text: How many distinct arrangements of $6$ different keys can be placed on a key ring, where reflections are considered identical?

options.why: Calculated (6 - 1)!, forgetting to divide by 2 for the key ring reflection.
Calculated 6! / 2 instead of (6 - 1)! / 2.
Calculated 6!, treating the keys as arranged in a distinct linear row.

questions.solution_text:
Arranging $6$ keys on a ring with reflections equivalent:
$= \dfrac{(6-1)!}{2}$
$= \dfrac{120}{2}$
$= 60$

questions.question_text: $8$ guests sit around a circular dining table. In how many ways can they sit if a specific married couple must sit together?

options.why: Forgot the 2! internal arrangement of the couple in their seating block.
Calculated unrestricted circular arrangements (8 - 1)! = 5040.
Multiplied by 4 instead of 2! for the internal couple arrangement.

questions.solution_text:
Treat couple as $1$ unit $\implies 7$ units in circle.
$= (7-1)! \times 2!$
$= 720 \times 2$
$= 1440$

questions.question_text: $6$ people sit around a circular table. In how many ways can they sit if $2$ particular people must NOT sit next to each other?

options.why: Calculated the number of arrangements where they DO sit together.
Calculated total unrestricted circular arrangements (6 - 1)! = 120.
Divided 120 by 2 assuming half of all circular arrangements separate them.

questions.question_text: $3$ boys and $3$ girls sit around a circular table. How many seating arrangements are possible if boys and girls alternate?

options.why: Multiplied by 2, confusing with the linear alternating formula.
Calculated linear alternating arrangements 2 times 3! times 3!.
Calculated only (3 - 1)! times 3 without permuting all girls as 3!.

questions.solution_text:
Fix $1$ boy ($1$). Arrange remaining $2$ boys: $(3-1)! = 2$.
Arrange $3$ girls in $3$ alternating spots: $3! = 6$.
$= 2 \times 6$
$= 12$

questions.question_text: $8$ delegates sit around a circular table, where rotations are considered equivalent. In how many ways can they be seated if Colin must sit directly between Alice and Brian?

options.why: Omitted the 2! internal arrangements of Alice and Brian on either side of Colin.
Calculated (6 - 1)! times 3! = 720, treating all 3 members as freely permutable.
Calculated unrestricted circular arrangements (8 - 1)! = 5040, ignoring the seating restriction.

questions.solution_text:
Treat Alice, Colin, and Brian as $1$ block with Colin in the middle.
Internal arrangements of Alice and Brian: $2! = 2$.
Arrange $6$ units around the table: $(6-1)! = 5! = 120$.
$= 120 \times 2$
$= 240$

questions.question_text: $9$ committee members sit around a circular table. In how many ways can they sit if $3$ specific members must sit together?

options.why: Forgot the 3! = 6 internal arrangements of the 3 people in the block.
Calculated unrestricted circular arrangements (9 - 1)! = 40320.
Multiplied by 3 instead of 3! = 6 for the internal block arrangement.

questions.solution_text:
Treat $3$ people as $1$ unit $\implies 7$ units in circle.
$= (7-1)! \times 3!$
$= 720 \times 6$
$= 4320$

questions.question_text: $6$ people sit around a circular table. In how many ways can they sit if Person A must sit directly opposite Person B?

options.why: Calculated (6 - 1)! = 120, ignoring the opposite seating condition.
Calculated (4 - 1)! = 6, treating remaining seats as circular.
Multiplied by 2, assuming A and B can swap after A fixes orientation.

questions.solution_text:
Fix Person A ($1$). Person B must sit directly opposite ($1$).
Arrange remaining $4$ people in remaining $4$ distinct seats:
$= 4!$
$= 24$
